claims.claim: Finite-sequence survival with unrotatable dominoes is in NP.
claims.evidence: For each explicitly listed fixed-orientation domino, a certificate gives its locking translation. Relative to the current explicit board, the legal translations in the board and constant-size spawn region form a directed graph of O(WH) vertices and constant outdegree. Exact graph reachability verifies access from spawn; support, loss, placement, and simultaneous full-row deletion are then deterministic polynomial-time checks. Any reachable translation has a simple path, so the certificate and verification over the whole explicit sequence are polynomial in the input size.
claims.search_method: Constructed the polynomial verifier directly and instantiated its fixed-orientation translation graph with exact finite searches.

claims.claim: For row-parallel unrotatable dominoes on an odd-width board, there is a computable linear-size upper bound on the number of pieces that can ever survive.
claims.evidence: Row deletion shifts every surviving row intact, so physical-row tokens are well defined. Before an initial token disappears, its original occupied cells permanently separate its original empty intervals. An interval of length l accepts at most floor(l/2) horizontal dominoes, and the token can become full only if every interval length is even. If C is the sum of these capacities and q is the number of parity-eligible initial tokens, only those q tokens can clear. Every resulting new top token starts empty, has odd width, can accept at most floor(W/2) dominoes, and can never clear because its occupied-cell count remains even. Hence every play has length at most U=C+q floor(W/2). Per row, capacity is at most floor(W/2), so U<=H(W-1), linear in the explicit board size. Exhaustive exact searches found no play of length U+1 in 5,528 small board/spawn instances.
claims.search_method: Proved the physical-token invariant and exhaustively searched all stable boards for selected odd sizes through W=7, using every possible horizontal spawn edge.

claims.claim: On an even-width board, two initially empty top rows suffice for survival of arbitrarily many row-parallel unrotatable dominoes.
claims.evidence: Partition the even number of columns into adjacent pairs. While the top two rows are empty, straight-dropping one domino into a pair makes the two column tops equal and locks no higher than the second row from the top, leaving the top row available for lateral access. If a row clears during this process, the untouched old top row plus the new top row restore the invariant. Otherwise, raise every shorter pair to the greatest pair height. The same access remains available, and when all pair tops reach that height, that row is full and clears. Thus every finite phase uses at least one piece, clears a row, and restores two empty top rows; repeating the phase gives one infinite play. The exact checker executed this construction successfully on 32,845 board/spawn instances through width 8.
claims.witness: The repeatable fixed-pair phase: seed every adjacent column pair, raise shorter pair stacks to the greatest pair top, and restart immediately after the guaranteed clear.
claims.search_method: Checked the invariant algebraically and exhaustively executed the constructive phase on all lower-row masks for the tested dimensions and every horizontal spawn edge.

claims.claim: The maximum survival length on an initially empty odd-width W×H board with row-parallel unrotatable dominoes is exactly H floor(W/2).
claims.evidence: Before a first clear, every row has even occupancy because every placement adds two cells to one row. An odd-width row therefore cannot be the first full row, so no clear ever occurs. Each row consequently contains at most floor(W/2) disjoint dominoes. For the matching lower bound, every edge of an odd path on W vertices belongs to a maximum matching of size floor(W/2): after selecting an edge, maximum matchings of the two residual paths complete it. Select such a matching containing the spawn edge and stack its edges identically from bottom to top. On the top row, place edges farthest-to-nearest on each side and the spawn edge last, preserving access. This realizes H floor(W/2) placements. For W=1 both sides are zero. Exact searches confirmed equality in 39 board/height/spawn instances through W=7 and H=3.
claims.witness: A maximum matching of the width-W row path containing the spawn edge, copied into every row and filled bottom-up, with the top-row spawn edge placed last.
claims.search_method: Completed the parity upper bound and matching construction, then exhaustively computed exact maxima for small odd empty boards over every spawn edge.

claims.claim: The row-capacity bound is not sufficient, and clearing one row does not guarantee indefinite unrotatable-domino survival.
claims.evidence: For the 3x3 board top/middle/bottom .../.#./..., the token calculation gives C=2, q=0, U=2, but every horizontal width-three position uses the center column. The middle obstruction forces the first domino to lock in the top row, and either top position intersects either possible spawn edge, so the exact maximum is one. Separately, on the 3x2 board .../..#, a domino in the two empty bottom cells clears that row and leaves an empty board. The empty odd-board result allows exactly two more pieces, making the total maximum three, not infinity. Exact reachability reproduced maxima 1 and 3 for both possible width-three spawn edges.
claims.witness: Capacity gap: .../.#./... on a 3x3 board. Finite after a clear: .../..# on a 3x2 board, first placing the domino in bottom columns 1-2.
claims.search_method: Enumerated every reachable lock and successor state with integer row masks for both concrete boards and both spawn edges.

claims.claim: Two initially empty top rows cannot in general be weakened to one on even-width row-parallel boards.
claims.evidence: On the 4x2 board top/bottom ..../#... with centered spawn columns 2-3, exact reachability gives only three first locks: bottom columns 2-3, bottom columns 3-4, or top columns 1-2. The top lock blocks the next spawn. Either bottom lock leaves no adjacent empty bottom pair, forcing the second domino to lock in the top row. Every horizontal top-row edge intersects centered spawn columns 2-3, so the third piece cannot spawn. A two-piece play exists, and exhaustive search confirms that no three-piece play exists.
claims.witness: The 4x2 initial board top/bottom = ..../#... with the horizontal spawn in columns 2-3; its exact maximum survival length is two.
claims.search_method: Enumerated the complete directed placement graph through three pieces and checked the three possible first locks exactly.

claims.claim: For odd-width row-parallel instances whose completely empty initial rows form a top prefix, finite clearing polynomial-time many-one reduces to finite survival.
claims.evidence: Let t be the number of initially empty top-prefix rows, R the remaining H-t nonempty tokens, m=floor(W/2), and K0 the sum of interval capacities in R. Clearing is impossible unless every interval in R is even and the input length K equals K0; immediate-NO cases can be mapped to the fixed NO survival instance consisting of the one-row board .#. and one horizontal domino. Otherwise, the token bound is C+qm=(K0+tm)+(H-t)m=K0+Hm. Map to survival on the same board for L=K0+Hm pieces. A clearing play extends by the empty-board construction for Hm pieces. Conversely, surviving L saturates the bound and forces every R token to clear. Empty-origin tokens always remain above R, so their placements support no retained lock; deleting those placements only removes obstacles and preserves the retained paths and clearing events. Equality also leaves exactly K0 retained placements, which clear R while all other tokens stay empty. The output length is O(WH). Exact enumeration confirmed the equivalence on 4,466 promised board/spawn instances, comprising 150 YES and 4,316 NO cases.
claims.witness: Reduction map: reject parity or K!=K0 cases to the fixed .#. one-piece NO instance; otherwise output the same board with a horizontal sequence of length K0+H floor(W/2).
claims.search_method: Proved both reduction directions via token saturation and deletion, and exhaustively compared exact clearing and survival reachability on small promised boards through width 5 and height 3.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a computational-complexity classification for the full finite unrotatable-domino survival problem. The draft proves NP membership and several substantive structural results for row-parallel or further promised instances, but supplies neither a polynomial-time algorithm nor an applicable NP-hardness reduction for every source-allowed instance. In particular, its clearing-to-survival reduction applies only at odd width with the top-prefix promise, and no hardness result for that promised clearing problem is established. Thus it makes correct material progress without resolving the requested classification. The draft labels its resolution PARTIAL and its final writeup expressly says the target remains unsettled, so that claimed resolution is accurate rather than overstated or understated.
